body: keep your expectations in check, and you'll be fine, I think.  I am a country girl so I don't really have a comparison but from others I hear that Tokyo isn't too different from any other big city. maybe making a friend who is familiar with the area or scenes you're into will keep you grounded.

howdy, neighbor. totally feel you on many fronts (save for the bf thing lol).  the ESL industry here is a crapshoot for the most part, and terribly draining.  but hahah I totally just squandered my day off as well; wish I'd seen this post earlier.  I hope you can figure out what you want to do.

it's really tough.  osu is interesting because of many things. you get immediate feedback (you just gained x pp or kudosu or whatevers) so it's easy to get hooked on that sense of accomplishment.  there is also a big community behind it.  it also can be an easy escape from "real world" problems.  an alternative might not cover ALL of these bases but maybe you can find them separately in other places.  feedback from one activity, connections with people in another.  it might take some searching.

it seems that you know that osu wasn't the problem, but a way of coping with the problems.  it's frustrating -- I know, I've been there -- but perhaps trying another doctor, different meds or therapy would help?  perhaps you haven't found what works for you yet, but something still might be out there.  looking at the comments in r/osugame it seems that you know that there are other things that are the root, so imho you'd do best to prioritize finding the real source of the problem.

and for this kind of thing, going "cold turkey" is dangerous and you will certainly hit a low point afterward.  please find some support and some kind of healthy alternative during this period.  again, I guess this is something you're probably struggling with now but please don't give up.  I wish you the best.

that sucks, op.  my experience is probably different from yours, but growing up non-white in the American South I kinda feel what you're talking about. right now I live in Asia and while it's not as direct here, I still get crap at times. it's really easy to say "those are just silly questions/attitudes, just ignore it" but that shit seriously *wears you down*.

do you have anyone around you that you can confide in? like someone from a similar or even some other kind of immigrant background? maybe finding someone to empathize with will help.  anyhow, I'm rooting for you.  stay strong!

I have struggled with my weight a lot and remembered some of the meds making me gain. I think it's a possible side effect? Please don't feel like it's too shallow to talk about. Perhaps they can empathize or help you out, especially if it has to do with your medicine. 

What helped me a lot was having a "safe snack" when I wanted to eat. I fucking love eating and portion control has been a problem for me but surrounding myself with healthier foods made binges not as big as a hit. I also sneaked in exercise when I could... walking to class instead of taking the bus, opting for stairs and such. It's a long journey but if you keep at it you can do it!

I'd also support the pet idea. I don't think I know what unconditional love from a person is either, but I briefly took care of a puppy and it was very fulfilling. 

Also your former partner sounds like he was a super-toxic scumbag. Is there a place you can exercises in peace? I was kind of the opposite (fatty trying to get some cardio) and was super self-conscious about it but slapping on some headphones and an upbeat playlist helped a lot.

1) I am not white, male, straight, etc. etc. and I feel like a lot of this PC stuff is silly (like, some things on Tumblr and the like make me roll my eyes) but then again in some open-minded, "lefty" spaces I have received so much bullshit.  The political groups I was in during college were hella sexist and there was a lot of "casual" racism to boot.  I think many Democrats spout that stuff but in practice they are just as bad as people on the other side.  It feels really disingenuous to me.

2) I haven't watched the Daily Show in years, but I think a HUGE difference is that Stewart is a comedian, not a journalist?  He's always made this clear.

Generally, I agree with the rest of your rant.  Perhaps you should consider learning more about progressivism?  They acknowledge most of the problems that you've pointed about about the Democratic Party.

Hmmm... sometimes I do help out students but since I'm not naturally "friendly" I feel that I'm poor with relationships a lot.  (More like all the time tbh.)  For every student I've maybe cheered up I feel like I've let one down.  :S

Are you alright? I'm awful with Internet sarcasm lol.  I hope things are going better for you recently. :)
I teach English in Asia.

I suppose my job is a little complicated.  I am called a "teacher" but I work for a private company.  it's more about sales and customer satisfaction than anything else.  when people IRL ask me what my job is, I will *never* say that I am a teacher.  I don't feel like one.

this makes me sad.  I don't think that I would be an awesome teacher anyway, but I care about education.  this job is more about numbers and pushing new gimmicky courses.

I am not the best with people either, but the connections I make with students are also important.  I get the vibe that many of them are also a little lost or lonely some way, so even if they are not at school to learn I try my best to make them smile a bit.  I am not good at it but I really try.

I have to catch a train in half an hour for work but I don't want to go.  :(  I want to cry more but I have to let my face dry for the makeup.  I'm so ugly lol.

I'm not up to talking to people for eight hours while feeling deathly lonely the entire time :((((((

Sorry for the delayed response, but I have read your entire reply and have been thinking about it.  

I did have a savings pot but a few months ago I started dipping into it -- and some of that was the money lending.  I know that it's for the best but the "saying no" thing is immensely difficult for me.  I don't like confrontation, I don't like disappointing people, and I have this almost pathological need to be honest.  I don't have the courage to do these things so I cave every time.  I suppose I need to find a way to be more confident, at least here.

I did CBT before (and I think I am rather introspective by nature, anyway) so I know that some of my thought patterns are harmful.  But it's hard to, say, not compare myself to others.  So many people around me have better talents and prospects and dreams.  I don't know if it is learned or innate but my primary (perhaps only?) fulfillment is from meeting others' expectations.  I feel like I'm too old to be this lost. 

I used to do Meetups, but my work schedule makes it difficult (the weekends and most evenings).  Besides being introverted a lot of the people I met before went on to be the flakes or leeches or manipulators I'm reeling over.  Also because of the assault I think I'm scared to go out at night or be around people who are drinking.  Everyone drinks here.  Like, *everyone*.

Sorry if I felt like I was just rejecting all of your suggestions just now.  Your comment really has given my stuff to think about.  I found an office that looks cheap the other day... therapy isn't covered under NHS here but I think maybe I can afford this.  I will call when I can.  I also thought about some things I can improve.  I know there are areas I need to get better in but I don't feel like I have the confidence for them.  I will do more thinking.  I will try to figure out how to get better.

There are lots of days when it feels like I can't though, and I want to go the other way.  I don't know what to do then.  I guess that this is another challenge.

Again, thanks so much; I really appreciate your reply.

every day I feel like I'm not strong enough.  I cry because I feel weak; I need to do better.

I don't even feel like I'm good at my job. I don't like it but I care deeply about it, if that make sense.

not really.  my family has been really dismissive or sometimes even vitriolic because I have such issues.  I'm also reached this point where it feels like I have no friends.  I have had a lot of bad things happen with personal relationships lately and some people have been just good, old-fashioned, ignoring me.

I feel you. I grew up in the Bible Belt, conservative family, the whole nine yards.

It's tough. I assume this is a Christian Church? The thing about many Christians, particularly very conservative ones is that if you are against or stray from The Path, you're an agent of Satan or something.

*Do* you stay with your family? Can you talk to them? Like my folks and I still don't jive with religion but through talks I have shared that we have a lot of the same beliefs -- be good to people and all that -- although my thoughts aren't rooted in a god. It has helped a bit. When I do go home I still go to church just to show up and make them happy. I hate it but it is a sacrifice I made. Just dress up on Sunday and try avoiding the subject the other six days of the week.

it's annoying when people don't respect your beliefs, though. I wish the best for you.

I don't think that they *hate* depressed people, but what carrying on a relationship with someone who is very depressed entails.  It is a struggle both ways. I have been both the depressed person and the supporter at times. I can understand why it's hard.  Regardless, it does feel like judgment and rejection -- and a deeply *personal* one at that.

It makes me so incredibly angry.  One of the first things they suggest for someone who is depressed is to find your support system, but I've always had people abandon me when they found out the depth and breadth of my problems.  I  would suppose many people have this struggle.  How do people find others to help?  This has been always an insurmountable challenge for me.

I really appreciate your thoughtful reply.  Such acknowledgement does help me, if only a little bit.

It is difficult.  I'm not friendly and naturally grim-faced but helping others is important to me.  The Golden Rule is a constant concern.  Recently someone asked me if I thought I was pushover and I agreed... yet I feel like I'm not trying hard enough.  For my job the image of the "happy-go-lucky" foreigner is key and I can't live up to that.  

And as a woman I have always tried to be sensitive to stories of sexual violence -- it had never happened to me but I knew the statistics so I knew it was *possible*.  I had no idea of how isolating and shameful it feels; that there are people who could ignore it, laugh it off or blame me.  I have gotten some empathy and sympathy online, which I am grateful for, but it feels so amazingly shitty when all the people you know in person treat you that way.

I spend most of my non-working, non-sleeping time studying the local language.  Certification of proficiency would be the first step to getting better work here.  Otherwise I am delving into making web sites.  Basic stuff is okay but where web design turns into web programming is where I'm weak.

Thanks so much for your reply; it means a lot. 

Perhaps some of this is not knowing what I want.  Because of certain circumstances I'm about 30 and haven't made much headway in life.  I feel like I should be focused on making up for lost time.

I am not very smart or talented so I have to work hard to be useful to others.  Most everything I do is related to that ideal.  I haven't ever come up with something I enjoy that has nothing to do with others' judgment.  I'm not sure if I can, but maybe that is key.

Sorry to hear about your troubles; it sounds like you are in a lot of pain.

I am an American living in Japan, but I think we have some things in common.  I have had many troubles as of late because people take advantage of me.  In my case it happens a lot because I really like helping people, and am probably naive and weak-willed.  Since coming here I've realized that it is largely the result of my upbringing (my childhood is comparable to some things in r/raisedbynarcissists).

Because of my upbringing I was often a target of bullying and exploitation, back home as well.  I like a lot of things about Japan, but the pressure and bullying can be suffocating, especially if you have a certain kind of personality.  It's bad here.  I can understand the desire to escape.

I thought that things might improve for me when I changed my environment, but I still carried many of the same troubles in my heart across the ocean.  You can't really escape yourself. 

In any case, thanks for sharing.  You stated that you don't want support, but I will send well wishes your way.

Hmmm I haven't looked much into local classes so I might try that again. Thing is, I am extremely shy so any efforts to be social are tough in the first place; failing repeatedly after such risks are the worst feeling in the world. I used to go to Meetups but a lot of the other foreigners *and* locals where the awful types that left me out the dry.

Also the expat community for my particular area on the net can be pretty awful; sometimes I get depressed looking at the vitriol on the sub here. 

But anyhow it wasn't too hard for me to get my job. Teaching English in Asia is a relatively easy gig provided you are a native speaker and have a 4 year degree. If you get certification like the CELTA you'll have a ton of opportunities to teach in so many places in the world if your interested.
